  kernel computes something, carries it correctly, and no code consumes it.

  FLYBYME/mesh-serve#1 landed  GET /api/_describe , gated  public , with  ETag
  and  304 , carrying  input ,  output ,  gate ,  destructive ,  errors  and  
   stream  for every exposed call. Nothing fetches it.                        
                                                                              
  A client should be able to obtain an  ApiSpec  from a live site rather than 
  only                                                                        
  from a build-time generated file.  spec/schema-driven-ui.md  §1 and §3.1 are
  the                                                                         
  design; read them before planning.                                          
                                                                              
  Carry  shapeHash , never the exposure hash —  net/client.ts:154  documents  
  why.                                                                        
                                                                              
  One bug to fix while you are there.  _describe  answers 409                 
  EXPOSURE_MISMATCH when the request carries an  x-exposure-shape  that       
  differs                                                                     
  from the server's. That is backwards for a discovery endpoint: the          
  descriptor is                                                               
  exactly what a stale client fetches in order to stop being stale, so        
  refusing                                                                    
  it is a recovery deadlock. It is unreachable today only because the client  
  reads                                                                       
  that header and never sends one. Do not start sending it on this call. If   
  you                                                                         
  believe the server side should change instead, open an issue against mesh-  
  serve                                                                       
  and say so — do not change it from here.                                    
                                                                              
  ## 2.  ctrl+alt+q : a full-screen log viewer                                
                                                                              
  Asked for twice.  kernel/broker.ts:418 's  makeLog  pushes into             
   services.logs , and  services.logs.push(...)  appears in  start.ts  at     
  lines                                                                       
  185, 423, 437, 450 and 518 and in  kernel.ts:163 .                          
                                                                              
  Six writers. No reader. Every  cx.log.info  from every part, every kernel   
  warning — manifest conflicts, mount failures, a part that did not start —   
  all                                                                         
  collected perfectly and displayed nowhere. Reported as "i believe there are 
  logs but i never see them."                                                 
                                                                              
  It must work on a site with no chrome.  window/page.ts:148  shows chrome is 
  optional and a site without it mounts the window layer at the root; the log 
  viewer is a kernel-level affordance, not a chrome feature. That is the whole
  reason it is a keybinding and not a button.                                 
                                                                              
  Mind  BROWSER_TAB_RESERVED  in  kernel/start.ts  — the existing defaults are
  chosen against it and  ctrl+alt+q  needs the same check.                    
                                                                              
  An unbounded array that only grows is a leak; decide the bound and say what 
  happens when it is hit.                                                     
                                                                              
  ## 3. A confirmation capability, so  destructive  has a reader              
                                                                              
   destructive: true  is declared on every contract that writes, travels in   
  the                                                                         
  descriptor, now reaches the browser — and nothing reads it.                 
                                                                              
  There is no way to ask a person "is this ok?" and wait.  Dialog  is a       
  primitive                                                                   
  that renders a  <dialog> ;  notifications  is a one-way signal array.       
  Neither                                                                     
  is                                                                          
  a decision.                                                                 
                                                                              
  A capability a contribution declares and the kernel provides: ask, and await
  an                                                                          
  answer. This is what makes a destructive call —  cdn.deploy  changes what a 
  hostname serves to the internet — confirmable without every screen inventing
  its                                                                         
  own modal.                                                                  
                                                                              
  Design it yourself and justify it. Two things it must get right: it is      
  declared like every other capability, so a site can see which parts can     
  interrupt the user; and it must be impossible for a caller to pretend the   
  user                                                                        
  answered. Do not wire it to  destructive  automatically in this PR — build  
  the                                                                         
  capability, note the intended consumer, and let the wiring be a decision

  daylight.
